title: Old Rules in the Valley
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：will　|　正文 304 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 will 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1963 nobody in the valley ① would sit in the doorway till dark, and every villager there remembered the fact for years. Three seasons on the world had turned over: by then even the youngest villager ② will sit in the doorway till dark in an hour, and nobody troubled to watch. My uncle wrote the change into the survey at once, and read the line aloud once every season thereafter.

The rules, though, were older than either of those worlds. A visitor ③ will not sit in the doorway till dark before the October rains; the ranger ④ would not sit in the doorway till dark either, and said so plainly to anybody who asked. Nobody in the valley ever thought of arguing with him about it.

⑤ Would anybody sit in the doorway till dark, my uncle wanted to know, without the ranger standing beside them? My mother, who heard every version of the story, said we ⑥ would sit in the doorway till dark once the survey was signed and not a day before. Even the oldest villager agreed with her in the end.

By 1969 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the survey: the work ⑦ will be finished before the October fair, and nothing was said otherwise. My uncle swore it ⑧ would have been finished long before anybody thought to ask. Would it truly have been finished so early? Nobody there could say.

⑨ In 1973 only one person in the whole valley would sit in the doorway till dark without help, and my mother kept the name in the survey for thirty years. ⑩ Even today a stranger will not sit in the doorway till dark without permission, and that, my mother said in 1975, is what the old rule was really about. She repeated the sentence whenever the valley forgot itself.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. modal. 将要（过去形式 would sit in the doorway till dark：1963 年那时候人人如此）
B. modal. 将要（现在形式 will sit in the doorway till dark：如今连最小的村民也一个钟头之内做得到）
C. modal. 总是（习性）（现在形式的否定 will not sit in the doorway till dark：规矩不许，如今也仍然如此）
D. modal. 将要（过去形式的否定 would not sit in the doorway till dark：那时的守林人也不能这么做）
E. modal. 将要（疑问句 would anybody sit in the doorway till dark?：叔叔当年追问的话）
F. modal. 将要（间接引语 she said we would sit in the doorway till dark：转述母亲的话）
G. modal. 将要（被动 will be finished：活儿被 finished 才算办妥）
H. modal. 将要（完成式 would have been finished：对早先情形的推断）

items.q: would sit in the doorway till dark
will sit in the doorway till dark in an hour
will not sit in the doorway till dark before
would not sit in the doorway till dark
would anybody sit in the doorway till dark,
we would sit in the doorway till dark once
would sit in the doorway till dark without help
will not sit in the doorway till dark without permission

answers.why: will 表将要，1963 年山谷里没有一个人在门口坐到天黑，叙述过去的事，故用过去形式 would。
will 表将要，多年之后连最年轻的村民都一个钟头之内在门口坐到天黑，说现在的情况，用 will。
will 表总是（习性），规矩上说客人不得在门口坐到天黑，否定形式是 will not sit in the doorway till dark。
will 表将要，守林人当年也不能这么做，过去形式的否定是 would not sit in the doorway till dark。
will 表将要，叔叔追问的是“难道没有人能在门口坐到天黑吗”，疑问句 would anybody sit in the doorway till dark?
will 表将要，母亲说的是“簿子签过之后我们才在门口坐到天黑”，间接引语里用 would。
will 表将要，踏勘记录上那行字是说活儿必须在集前被人 finished，被动形式 will be finished。
will 表将要，叔叔断定活儿老早就被 finished，对过去的推断用 would have been finished。
will 表将要，1973 年只有一个人无人相助也能在门口坐到天黑，用过去形式 would。
will 表总是（习性），母亲 1975 年说，如今生人没有许可仍不得在门口坐到天黑，否定 will not sit in the doorway till dark。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1963 年，山谷里没有一个人在门口坐到天黑，人人都把这件事记了好多年。（would sit in the doorway till dark）
多年以后，连最年轻的村民都一个钟头之内在门口坐到天黑。（will sit in the doorway till dark）
按老规矩，客人在十月雨季之前不得在门口坐到天黑。（will not sit in the doorway till dark）
那位守林人当年也不能在门口坐到天黑，谁问他就直说。（would not sit in the doorway till dark）
母亲说，簿子签过之后我们才可以在门口坐到天黑，早一天也不行。（she said we would sit in the doorway till dark）
叔叔一口咬定，那件活儿早在有人过问之前就被 finished 了。（would have been finished）

Three seasons on, even the youngest villager will sit in the doorway till dark in an hour.

The ranger would not sit in the doorway till dark either, and said so plainly to anybody who asked.
